name: Promotional workplace title inflation
description: Recruitment and workplace praise borrowing celebrity, magic, and franchise terminology to imply exceptional competence.
cause_of_death: Recruitment-search friction and explicit professional backlash; several terms resurged, so terminal fades remain estimates.

sources.title: May the 4th Be With You: Jedi and Other Weird Job Titles on Indeed
sources.note: Reports Indeed data: guru decline after July 2012, oscillating wizard use, slight rockstar decline, and renewed ninja/Jedi growth.

sources.title: Calling all Time Ninjas: let's put a stop to ludicrous job titles
sources.note: Contemporary critique of alienating and infantilizing job-title suffixes; not evidence of complete extinction.

sources.title: Are you really looking for a Guru, Rock Star or Ninja?
sources.note: Contemporary recruitment criticism; HTML datePublished metadata directly confirms publication on 2013-01-25 although the visible page does not display it.

sources.title: Ninja sneaks up on competition in Indeed's Weird Job Titles 2018 report
sources.note: Counterevidence: ninja and rockstar grew in 2018; wizard and hero declined. Prevents a false 2016-extinction claim.

entries.gloss: A recruitment and workplace compliment casting ordinary professional competence as celebrity performance.

examples.text: You are a rockstar for covering my shift; thank you.

entries.rationale: The 2013 recruitment critique attests the label; Indeed reports slight decline in May 2016 but 17% growth in 2018. The estimated 2015 peak and 2020 fade delimit the initial promotional/backlash register, not a monotonic measured history or extinction.

entries.gloss: A recruitment and workplace label for supposedly exceptional speed and covert proficiency.

examples.text: Could you be a printout ninja and bring those pages to the meeting?

entries.rationale: A 2013 critique and 2016 Indeed report establish the register and a second-half-2015 decline. Ninja rebounded and grew 90% in 2018, so the peak/fade are an estimated first-wave register envelope rather than a measured single historical maximum.

entries.gloss: An inflated occupational label claiming authoritative professional mastery.

examples.text: Thank you, scheduling guru, for covering my shift.

entries.rationale: Indeed's May 2016 report specifically dates high keyword popularity until July 2012 followed by steep decline. The onset and terminal fade are estimated; persistent and later job advertisements are explicitly acknowledged.

entries.gloss: A workplace label casting ordinary expertise as magical problem-solving ability.

examples.text: You are a printout wizard; thank you for bringing every page.

entries.rationale: Indeed ties oscillation to the last Harry Potter movie in 2011; 2013 recruitment criticism attests Numbers Wizard, and HR Dive reports a 17% drop in 2018. Boundaries interpolate these observations and do not establish a complete measured disappearance.

entries.gloss: A branded recruitment metaphor for exceptional technical or professional ability.

examples.text: Could you apply your scheduling Jedi skills and arrange Friday coverage?

entries.rationale: The 2016 Indeed report observes 328% growth after the previous year's Star Wars release and recommends factual titles. This is an explicitly estimated release-linked flare, with an inferred 2020 fade rather than an observed last use.
